method: Assisted abstract review supplied as external notes; no model or retrieval API calls.

25178568.rationale: A 12-month randomized comparison reports fat-mass differences. Diet and timing differ from the exact claim; the percent fat-mass contrast must not be reported as kilograms or absolute fat loss.

26278052.rationale: Six-day randomized-order isocaloric feeding comparison estimates body-fat loss using fat balance. It does not test the exact food list, and does not establish the necessity of excluding grains/dairy.

28676132.rationale: Systematic review of mostly observational pediatric evidence on ultra-processed foods and body fat. Associations in children/adolescents do not establish the effect of switching to the prescribed diet.

31105044.rationale: Two-week randomized feeding comparison reports energy intake and weight in this abstract, not body-fat change. Follow linked errata before relying on numerical results; missing abstract endpoints may exist in full text.

32990607.rationale: Randomized study in NAFLD reports two-month body-fat decreases within the intervention group. A between-group fat-loss effect is not explicitly reported in the abstract. Diet includes high fiber and education and is not the exact food list.

33479499.rationale: Randomized two-week feeding periods compare energy intake. The abstract does not report a body-fat result; this is not evidence that the full study lacks one. One participant withdrew due to hypoglycemia during the low-carbohydrate diet.

33802738.rationale: Secondary analysis relates diet adherence to lower fat mass at 12 weeks in T2D. Participants were randomized to exercise conditions, not to high versus low Paleo adherence; do not treat adherence associations as randomized diet effects.

33916669.rationale: Narrative review discusses short-term fat-mass reduction and longer-term limitations of LCD. It is neither a new trial nor an exact assessment of the video diet. Safety assertions require checking underlying evidence.

34515299.rationale: Conceptual carbohydrate-insulin model with testable hypotheses; not an intervention effect estimate or established demonstration of rapid fat loss.

35362512.rationale: Mostly observational pediatric systematic review includes percentage-body-fat associations, low certainty, heterogeneous exposures. Not a trial of the prescribed diet; linked erratum requires review before using estimates.

36313106.rationale: Long-term UPF/body-composition association in a cohort, with reported associations only in women. Not rapid fat loss following randomized diet substitution.

37296485.rationale: Position statement directly useful for reviewing quick-loss promises, food-group exclusions and energy deficit. Critical guidance is relevant but not an experimental refutation of the exact claim.

37535715.rationale: Short abstract lists possible obesity drivers and discusses weight-loss drugs; it supplies no dietary fat-loss effect or focused assessment of the claimed restriction.

40760353.rationale: Eight-week minimally processed versus UPF feeding periods report weight-change outcomes. Primary endpoint is weight, not body fat in this abstract. Both diets follow Eatwell guidance and do not establish necessity of the video exclusions.

40933253.rationale: Diet comparison targets glycemia while maintaining stable weight. No fat-loss estimate is reported in the abstract. Stable weight must not be interpreted as proof of zero body-fat change.

41628734.rationale: Cancer nutrition review does not evaluate whether the prescribed restriction produces rapid body-fat loss. Shared food vocabulary is insufficient.

42502137.rationale: MASLD lifestyle overview concerns weight management and hepatic disease. It reports no evaluation of rapid whole-body fat loss from the exact restriction in the abstract.
